title: What is known about 1RB---_1RC0LD_0LB0RE_1LB1LC_1RD1RF_1RD1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1RC0LD_0LB0RE_1LB1LC_1RD1RF_1RD1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Its tape is written in two words, 10 and 110, and holds a few counters. For most of the time it runs a simple loop: each cycle moves the head across the tape and back, adds six 10s to one block and one 110 to another, and removes two 10s from a third. When the third block is empty, a messier transition phase sets up the next loop with blocks about 3.9 times longer.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

Where a halt would come from. The machine halts only in state A reading 1, which needs C to read a 1 followed by three more 1s: C, E, F and A then each read a 1 in turn. A tape made of 10 and 110 never has three 1s in a row; only the transition phases write longer blocks of 1s, and C has never met one.
What a proof needs. The main loop is an exact linear rule and should be provable for all block sizes; the transition phase between loops is not yet understood well enough to state as a rule.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 6,110 cells have been visited and 3,396 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The main loop
claims.text: Each time B is at the left end with tape B>0 0 (10)^x 0 10 (110)^y (10)^z 0 10 (110)^c 1, the next such time has (x + 6, y + 1, z − 2, c). In the first 109 steps this holds for 451 of the 453 consecutive pairs; the other two are phase changes. The steps per cycle grow by 180 from one cycle to the next.

claims.title: Growing phases
claims.text: Loops start at (x, y, z, c) = (10, 1, 80, 18) at step 256,267, (10, 1, 319, 71) at step 8,230,627, and (10, 1, 1232, 274) at step 501,539,030: z and c grow by a factor near 3.9 per phase. A loop runs until z is used up (about z/2 cycles); then a transition phase, in which the tape holds long blocks of 1s, builds the next loop.

claims.title: C never sees four 1s
claims.text: Halting needs C to read a 1 with three 1s to its right. In 10<sup>9</sup> steps C reads a 1 166,617,942 times; the run of 1s right of it has length 0 (214,443 times), 1 (166,260,677 times) or 2 (142,822 times), never 3.
claims.where: windows when C and F read 1

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.274). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The main loop is regular, but the transition between loops is not understood exactly.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine moves numbers between counters written in 10s and 110s, in phases that grow about four-fold each time. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Each cycle of the main loop changes three block lengths by fixed amounts.
Each loop starts with blocks about 3.9 times longer than the last.

sections.heading: Three counters and a loop
html: Most of the tape is written in two words, a = 10 and b = 110. Stop the run when the head is at the left end in state B and you usually see
B>0 0 a^x 0 a b^y a^z 0 a b^c 1

and at the next such moment x has grown by 6, y by 1, and z has shrunk by 2, while c stays put. For example at step 501,539,693 the tape is B>0 0 a^16 0 a b^2 a^1230 0 a b^274 1. Each cycle the head crosses the blocks and comes back, so a cycle takes time proportional to the width, and the cycles get 180 steps longer each time.

sections.heading: Phases that grow
html: The loop runs until z, the block being drained, is empty: then a transition phase takes over, during which the tape contains long blocks of 1s and changes in a less regular way, and it ends by setting up a new loop with longer blocks. The loops start at (x, y, z, c) = (10, 1, 80, 18), (10, 1, 319, 71) and (10, 1, 1232, 274), at steps 256,267, 8,230,627 and 501,539,030. The blocks grow by about 3.9 per phase and the time by much more, so the tape grows like a small power of the time: 6,110 cells after 109 steps.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The halting transition is A reading 1. A is entered only from F reading 1, F only from E reading 1, and E only from C reading 1, each stepping right. So a halt needs C on a run of four 1s. A tape of 10s and 110s never has three 1s in a row; long blocks of 1s appear only in the transition phases, and so far C has never stood at the start of four of them.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.274). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 6,110 cells (4,198 left of the start, 261 right), with a density of 1s of 0.556.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: three-counter transfer machine in growing phases
summary: Tape of 10s and 110s holding three counters; in long phases one counter is drained into the other two at fixed rates (+6, +1, −2 per cycle), and each phase sets up the next about 3.9 times larger.
